themes.title: Operations the C++ class deletes
themes.note: A deleted copy constructor or assignment operator has no behavior to expose. Its absence from the C ABI is the same statement the C++ class already makes.

themes.title: C++ iterators and range-for support
themes.note: An iterator has no fixed size, no stable representation and no C spelling. Every collection this ABI exposes is iterated as a count plus indexed access, or through an explicit enumerator handle where the canonical type has one.

themes.title: Protected members with no derived class to hang them on
themes.note: A protected member is mappable only when this ABI supplies a derived class that would override it. Where it does -- a game component's hooks -- the member is mapped; where the derived class is the caller's C++ code, there is nothing for C to override.

themes.title: Templates over an arbitrary C++ type
themes.note: C cannot name a C++ type, so a generic operation cannot be called from C at all. Where the canonical template has a small closed set of useful instantiations, the ABI names them one by one instead; the generic form itself stays unmapped.

themes.title: Values that are Sharp Runtime objects
themes.note: Sharp Runtime is an implementation dependency and never a C type. An operation whose value *is* such an object has nothing to hand across the boundary; see SHARP_RUNTIME_BOUNDARY.md.

themes.title: Raw native backend pointers
themes.note: A route that accepts or returns an SDL pointer would make the caller's program depend on CNA's backend choice, which is the one thing this ABI exists to prevent.

themes.title: Friendship declarations
themes.note: A friend declaration grants a canonical CNA type access to another's internals. It declares no callable operation.

themes.title: Declared and never defined in CNA itself
themes.note: Not a design choice: the canonical declaration has no definition anywhere in CNA, so there is nothing to bind. CApi_UnimplementedRuntimeFacade keeps that record from going stale in silence.

themes.title: Objects the caller never constructs or destroys
match: every method that produces one is private
the only collection that means anything
themes.note: Where CNA owns the only instance and its lifetime, the constructor and destructor are not operations a caller can perform, so they are not routes.

themes.title: C++ language mechanics with no runtime behavior
match: no second name to move from
themes.note: Aliases, markers, move semantics and destructors that exist for the C++ type system. C holds every object by handle and never deletes through an interface.

themes.title: Asynchronous-result objects nothing produces
themes.note: The canonical asynchronous pair completes before its Begin returns, so the C route is a single call that invokes the callback. The result object itself is never handed out.

themes.title: Canonical routes this ABI declines to bind
match: constraint the canonical source states outright
real limitation rather than an oversight
themes.note: A small number of canonical operations are unsafe or meaningless when reached through a C handle. Binding them would hand a caller a way to corrupt memory or to observe an event that can never fire; each is recorded individually in COVERAGE.md.

environment.subject: FFmpeg stays a system dependency
environment.impact: The package installs the SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer libraries this project builds, beside `libcna_c_api.so`, whose RPATH is `$ORIGIN` -- so an installed CNA links and runs with no environment variable. FFmpeg is different: libavcodec, libavformat, libavutil and libswresample come from the distribution. Copying a distribution's binaries into this package would take on their redistribution terms, freeze their soname against future security updates and drag in the transitive libraries they were linked against, so they remain a system dependency a deployment installs the ordinary way.

environment.subject: There is no static configuration
environment.impact: `CNA_C_API_STATIC` names a future configuration that does not exist. A static build would export every C++ symbol it archived, and the ABI promise -- 2,720 `cna_*` names and nothing else -- would be meaningless.

environment.subject: One active CNA runtime per process
environment.impact: A second `cna_game_create` while a game is alive returns `CNA_RESULT_INVALID_STATE`. This makes the interaction with CNA's process-level graphics and input state explicit; simultaneous runtimes are an ABI-semantic change requiring a reviewed design.

environment.subject: Handles are thread-affine and never leave their process
environment.impact: A handle used from a thread other than its creator's answers `CNA_RESULT_THREAD`. Handles are not pointers, not serializable and not stable across processes.

environment.subject: The ABI is 0.x and experimental
environment.impact: An incompatible change requires only a minor-version increment, release notes and a regenerated baseline. The additive-only guarantee begins at 1.0, which is a separate, later decision.

environment.subject: Four of the 46 renderers are built and run here
environment.impact: The other 42 share the same C surface and the same capability queries. What a given backend supports is answered by `cna_graphics_device_supports_capability`, never by its renderer identity.
